headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said the AI industry should accept no cybersecurity incidents caused by AI and told those who fear AI will end civilisation to stop working on it.
score_reason: Pool score kept: on-record interview that opens a public split with OpenAI's chief executive; opinion, not new action.
importance_line: Two of the industry's most prominent chief executives now disagree in public on whether AI-caused hacks are an acceptable price, which bears on how fast rules and containment tools are demanded, though Huang's view is also the view of a company that sells the chips.
summary: Fortune reports that Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, told it in London "We should not accept any" AI-caused cybersecurity incidents, putting him at odds with Sam Altman, chief executive of OpenAI, who told Vanity Fair earlier this month that the world may have to accept "some bad things happening" for AI's benefits and later told Politico's Decoded podcast of "a coming tidal wave of cybersecurity problems" from rival open-source models. Huang said the incidents so far could have been avoided by sealing AI agents in secure containers, and that people who believe AI will end human civilisation "really ought to stop working on it."
notes: Reply story: Huang answers Altman's Vanity Fair and Politico Decoded remarks (dates of those interviews given only as 'earlier this month' and 'subsequent'). Not previously carried in our editions as far as the 14 Oct title list shows.
